Where it began

Usman Khawaja was born in Islamabad on 18 December 1986, and was four when the family settled in New South Wales. He went to Westfields Sports High School in Fairfield West and opened the batting for Australia at the 2006 Under-19 World Cup in Sri Lanka.

He first played first-class cricket for New South Wales in 2008, the year he made double hundreds in successive second XI games, a first for the state.

The player

His Test debut came in the Ashes at Sydney on 3 January 2011, which made him the first Australian of Pakistani origin to play Test cricket for his country. His first Test hundred, 174 against New Zealand, had to wait until November 2015, and the years around it were stop and start.

The second act was the best. Recalled for the Sydney Ashes Test in January 2022, he made a hundred in each innings, then went to Pakistan, the land of his birth, and scored 496 runs at 165.33 to be player of the series. A career-best 195 against South Africa followed, then 141 at Edgbaston in the 2023 Ashes, a match in which he batted on all five days. In Galle in January 2025 he made 232, the first Test double hundred by an Australian in Sri Lanka. He played his last Test at Sydney in January 2026, as Australia took the Ashes 4-1. In all he played 88 Tests from 2011 to 2026, scoring 6,229 runs at 42.96 with 16 hundreds and 28 fifties, and holding 68 catches.

What made him special

He was a left-hander of rare calm, with the patience to bat for days and the grace to make it look easy. Spin bowling, for a while, was the one puzzle he had not solved, until a match-saving 141 in Dubai in 2018, opening in the fourth innings, showed how far he had come. In 2025 he became the only Australian with Test hundreds in India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and the United Arab Emirates.

He was part of the side that won the 2021–2023 World Test Championship, and was named the ICC's Test Cricketer of the Year for 2023, and won Australia's own Shane Warne award for the best Test player of that season. Wisden made him one of its Cricketers of the Year in 2024.

Away from the middle

Khawaja is a qualified commercial pilot, rated to fly on instruments, who had an aviation degree from the University of New South Wales in his pocket before he ever played a Test. He held a pilot's licence before he had one to drive a car. At home he captained Queensland to the Sheffield Shield in 2020–21, and top-scored with 70 when the Sydney Thunder won the Big Bash League final of 2015–16.

And finally

Before his first Test against Pakistan, at the Gabba in December 2016, he went looking for someone to unlock the changing rooms. A kind member of staff obliged and set off towards the visitors' dressing room. He had to point her, very politely, the other way.
